macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks close lower as inflation and Fed-hike concerns persist
items.summary: The Dow fell 0.36%, the S&P 500 declined 0.35% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.39%. Investors remained focused on elevated inflation, rising Treasury yields and the possibility of another Federal Reserve rate increase.[7]

items.title: Fed officials signal further tightening may be needed
items.summary: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said additional policy tightening may be necessary because inflation remains persistent and businesses are increasingly prepared to pass higher input costs to consumers.[7]

items.title: Markets await U.S. producer-price inflation data
items.summary: Investors are awaiting the Producer Price Index after hotter-than-expected consumer inflation and higher energy costs strengthened expectations that the Fed could maintain or increase policy rates.[1][2]

items.title: Treasury yields and oil prices surge
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.10%, while Brent crude gained 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel amid renewed geopolitical tensions, adding to inflation concerns.[4][7]

items.title: Nvidia shares fall after leadership shake-up
items.summary: Nvidia dropped 4.3% after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was ousted, while investors reassessed the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade.[7][8]

items.title: Cisco and Applied Materials raise forecasts
items.summary: Cisco reported roughly $18.1 billion in quarterly revenue and increased its full-year guidance. Applied Materials forecast approximately $11.10 billion in fiscal first-quarter revenue, above the analyst consensus cited by LSEG.[2]

items.title: Cerebras posts strong growth and outlook
items.summary: Cerebras reported third-quarter core revenue of $230.9 million, up 70% year over year, and issued a next-quarter revenue forecast above expectations; its shares rose more than 16% after hours.[4]

items.title: Yen weakens beyond 160 per dollar
items.summary: The yen fell past 160 per dollar for the first time since September, putting renewed focus on currency-market intervention risks and global interest-rate differentials.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $70,000 as crypto sell-off intensifies
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped sharply, reaching roughly $67,600 and losing more than 8% over 24 hours. Ether and BNB also declined, while leveraged liquidations were concentrated among long positions.

items.title: Crypto liquidations exceed $1 billion as Bitcoin tests multi-week lows
items.summary: Bitcoin reportedly fell about 5%–6% during Thursday trading to a low near $74,800, with more than $1 billion in predominantly long-position liquidations. The move followed weakness in technology and AI-related equities.

items.title: Thailand proposes daily stablecoin transaction caps
items.summary: Thailand’s securities regulator proposed separate daily limits of approximately $148,000 for stablecoin deposits and withdrawals, along with a requirement that users transact through wallets they own.

items.title: U.S. regulators receive nominees for vacant SEC and CFTC seats
items.summary: President Donald Trump nominated four people to fill vacant commissioner positions at the SEC and CFTC, potentially reshaping U.S. oversight of cryptocurrency markets.

items.title: U.S. Treasury develops custody framework for government-held Bitcoin
items.summary: The Treasury is reportedly working on standardized custody procedures for Bitcoin held by government agencies, including seized assets and holdings associated with the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.

items.title: Project Faro secures $270 million for bank-backed stablecoin venture
items.summary: Goldman Sachs, Citi and other banks reportedly committed $270 million to fund five years of operations for Project Faro, a stablecoin initiative involving 21 financial institutions and targeting a dollar-based launch in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Coinbase receives approval for National Trust Company
items.summary: Coinbase launched a National Trust Company after receiving final approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, expanding its federally supervised digital-asset custody operations.

items.title: NYSE selects Avalanche for tokenized-securities settlement infrastructure
items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange reportedly selected Avalanche as the core clearing and settlement layer for a planned 24/7 tokenized-securities platform, subject to regulatory approval.

items.title: Crypto hacking losses reach $8.7 billion in 2026
items.summary: ARK research cited by Cointelegraph estimated that crypto hackers had stolen $8.7 billion so far in 2026, an amount exceeding projected annual on-chain industry revenue.

items.title: Gnosis Pay reports sensitive-data breach
items.summary: Gnosis Pay reportedly suffered a data breach exposing sensitive information, including names, addresses, banking details and linked crypto addresses; no loss of funds was reported.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GDC report finds layoffs remain a major industry problem
items.summary: A new GDC industry report says 34% of surveyed game professionals were laid off during the past 24 months, rising to 39% among U.S.-based respondents. More than half of those laid off have not found another job, while generative-AI use in development continues to increase.

items.title: MachineGames confirms Wolfenstein 3 is in development
items.summary: MachineGames has officially confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is in active production, ending years of speculation about the future of the first-person shooter franchise.

items.title: Microsoft expands original Xbox games on PC
items.summary: Microsoft has added 21 original Xbox titles to its PC backward-compatibility program, including TimeSplitters 2, The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, and several Star Wars games.

items.title: Dark Souls 2 and 3 online servers return
items.summary: FromSoftware has restored online multiplayer services for Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 after nearly two weeks of downtime.

items.title: Paradox Interactive CEO Fredrik Wester steps down
items.summary: Fredrik Wester is leaving his position as CEO of Paradox Interactive for the second time. The company is known for strategy series including Crusader Kings, Stellaris, and Cities: Skylines.

items.title: Le Mans Ultimate surpasses two million unit sales
items.summary: Motorsport Games reported that Le Mans Ultimate has sold more than two million combined base-game and downloadable-content units. The racing game also reached a record 11,941 concurrent players during an October special event.

items.title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet enters final development stage
items.summary: Naughty Dog head Neil Druckmann said the studio’s sci-fi action game Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is fully playable and in the final polishing stage of development.

items.title: Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+ coming to Apple Arcade
items.summary: Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+ is scheduled to launch on Apple Arcade on December 3.

items.title: Xbox CEO marks 25th anniversary and outlines future
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma issued a statement commemorating Xbox’s 25th anniversary and discussing the brand’s future direction.

items.title: Scotland’s game industry remains active despite wider pressures
items.summary: A BBC report examines Scotland’s video game sector, highlighting its continuing activity and recent projects including Silent Hill: Townfall, while considering the broader challenges facing game development.
